cover: When your spreadsheet should become a database

slides.title: Size is rarely the reason
slides.body: Excel allows over a million rows per sheet. Most business spreadsheets get into trouble long before that.

slides.title: The same record, three versions
slides.body: One customer in several tabs or files, and they don't agree. Nobody knows which one is right.

slides.title: Nobody knows who changed it
slides.body: A spreadsheet can't show who edited a number or when, so a wrong figure has nothing to settle it.

slides.title: A database enforces the rules
slides.body: A status comes from a fixed list. An order needs a real customer. A rushed edit can't quietly break that.

slides.title: Start with the data model
slides.body: Screens can change in a week. A database with years of records in it is much harder to restructure.
